scope_notes: Covers the block start/set position, acceleration (first ~10-30 m) and maximal-velocity mechanics incl. arm action. Bend running, relays and hurdles are not covered.
source_gap_notes: Well supported by peer-reviewed reviews (sprint start, acceleration, max velocity) and World Athletics biomechanics reports; drill content comes from Vince Anderson (Texas A&M / USATF coaching education) and SimpliFaster. USATF coach-education manuals themselves are not freely available online.

sources.name: Bezodis NE, Willwacher S, Salo AIT - The Biomechanics of the Track and Field Sprint Start: A Narrative Review (Sports Medicine 2019)
sources.credibility: Authoritative review of block set-up, block phase and first steps.

sources.name: Biomechanical Performance Factors in the Track and Field Sprint Start: A Systematic Review (IJERPH 2022)
sources.credibility: Systematic review: rapid hip extension, strong rear-leg force, short first flight and longer first stance associated with better starts.

sources.name: Alt T et al. - A novel guideline for the analysis of linear acceleration mechanics: 'shin roll' (Sports Biomechanics 2022)
sources.credibility: Conceptual framework with 4 key positions (shin block, touchdown, heel lock, propulsion pose) for sagittal video analysis of acceleration.

sources.name: Sportsmith - 'Shin roll' and its importance in acceleration (interview with Tobias Alt)
sources.credibility: Author of SP3 explains assessment (>=100 fps, camera 6-10 m away), drills and cues.

sources.name: Haugen T et al. - The Training and Development of Elite Sprint Performance (Sports Medicine - Open 2019)
sources.credibility: Integrates science and best practice: max velocity determinants, training doses (e.g., 20-40 m flying sprints).

sources.name: Haugen T, McGhie D, Ettema G - Sprint running: from fundamental mechanics to practice - a review (Eur J Appl Physiol 2019)
sources.credibility: Review of sprint mechanics (ground contact, step rate/length, force application). DOI from SP4's reference list.

sources.name: Morin JB, Edouard P, Samozino P - Technical ability of force application as a determinant of sprint performance (MSSE 2011)
sources.credibility: Ability to orient ground force horizontally distinguishes better accelerators. DOI from SP4's reference list.

sources.name: Vince Anderson - Three Foundational Exercises Explained (Ins & Outs, Acceleration/Stick drill, V-Max Wicket drill)
sources.credibility: Texas A&M sprint/hurdle coach; originator of the modern wicket drill; USATF Level 2 school lineage.

sources.name: SimpliFaster - How to Improve Front-Side Mechanics and Force Production with the Wicket Drill
sources.credibility: Widely read coaching publication; wicket drill set-up and rationale.

sources.name: World Athletics - Biomechanical Report, Men's 100m, 2017 IAAF World Championships London
sources.credibility: Official step length/frequency data for elite finalists.

skills.name: Block start and set position
skills.recommended_camera: Side view, camera perpendicular at hip height ~6-10 m away, >=100 fps (ideally 240).

checkpoints.description: Set position: hips rise slightly above shoulder height; shoulders over or slightly in front of the hands; weight forward onto the hands.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hip height > shoulder height; shoulder x-position at or ahead of wrists

checkpoints.description: Front-leg knee roughly 90 deg and rear-leg knee more open (~110-135 deg) in the set position (commonly reported ranges; individualize).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: front knee ~85-100 deg; rear knee ~110-135 deg

checkpoints.description: Block clearance: forceful extension pushing BOTH blocks, rapid hip extension and a strong rear-leg push.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: front leg reaches near-full extension at block exit; trunk forms a straight line with the push leg

checkpoints.description: First steps are short with a low flight time and a relatively long first stance; feet land behind/under the hips, not out in front.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: first touchdown foot position at or behind the hip vertical; short flight before first contact

faults.name: Popping up out of the blocks
faults.video_signs: Trunk rises quickly to upright in the first 1-2 steps; head lifts.
faults.correction_cue: 'Push, don't jump - stay low and let the body rise gradually.'
faults.why_it_matters: Rising early directs force vertically instead of horizontally.

faults.name: Reaching first step
faults.video_signs: First foot lands well in front of the hips; braking visible.
faults.correction_cue: 'Step down under the hips - piston the legs.'
faults.why_it_matters: Landing in front of the centre of mass creates braking.

faults.name: Weak rear-leg push / single-leg start
faults.video_signs: Rear foot leaves the block almost immediately with little push.
faults.why_it_matters: Rear-leg force contributes significantly to block velocity.

drills.name: Block clearance to 3-5 steps
drills.setup: Blocks set to the athlete's measured spacing; film from the side at >=100 fps.
steps: Set position: check hips above shoulders, knee angles.
On the command, push BOTH blocks and drive out low.
Run only 3-5 steps, focusing on feet landing under/behind the hips.
Review video for block exit posture and first-step placement.
drills.fixes: Popping up; reaching first step; weak rear-leg push
drills.why: Short reps keep quality maximal on the variables reviews associate with good starts: strong push from both legs, short first flight, feet landing behind the hips.

pro_tips.tip: Different whole-body strategies can produce similar start times - use the research ranges as guides, not rigid rules.

skills.name: Acceleration (drive phase)
skills.recommended_camera: Side view, perpendicular, camera 6-10 m away, >=100 fps (per Alt/Sportsmith).

checkpoints.description: Forward lean that rises gradually over the first ~10-30 m; push leg, trunk and head roughly in line at toe-off.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: trunk lean from vertical decreases progressively step by step (e.g., ~45 deg at step 1 rising toward upright by ~30 m)

checkpoints.description: Shin roll: the shin rotates forward progressively from late swing (shin block) through stance to the propulsion pose; positive (forward-inclined) shin angle at touchdown in early steps.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: shin-to-ground angle decreases from shin block -> touchdown -> heel lock -> propulsion pose; measure at each key frame

checkpoints.description: Foot touches down near/under (slightly behind) the centre of mass in early steps, minimizing braking.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: touchdown ankle at or slightly behind the hip vertical during the first ~6-8 steps

checkpoints.description: Big, aggressive arm action ('hard splits with the hands').
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: large shoulder flexion/extension amplitude; hands don't cross the midline

faults.name: Overstriding / reaching in acceleration
faults.video_signs: Foot lands well in front of the hips with the shin vertical or angled back.
faults.correction_cue: 'Push the ground behind you - rock and roll.'
faults.why_it_matters: Reaching causes braking and wastes the horizontal force needed to accelerate.

faults.name: Excessive vertical bounce
faults.video_signs: Hips rise quickly; looks like bounding upward rather than driving forward.
faults.why_it_matters: Accelerating requires patience to rotate the COM forward rather than lifting it.

faults.name: Bent-at-the-waist lean
faults.video_signs: Lean comes from hip flexion (bent over) rather than a straight line from ankle to head.
faults.correction_cue: 'Lean from the ankles - straight line from heel to head.'
faults.why_it_matters: Posture before power: forces can only be expressed well if segments are aligned.

drills.name: Acceleration 'stick' (tape) drill
drills.setup: Lay sticks/tape marks starting ~0.65 m from the start line and increasing ~0.15 m per stride (adjust to the athlete). Provide 2-3 lanes with different spacings.
steps: Start from a crouch or 3-point stance.
Accelerate hitting each space with a push, not a reach.
Ask: 'Where did you feel yourself stop pushing and start running?'
Progress from grass to track, flats to spikes, then add resistance/hills.
drills.dosage: 2-3 x (10, 20, 30 m); total 120-300 m; rest ~1 min per 10 m
drills.why: Marks enforce progressively lengthening steps so the athlete must push longer and harder instead of reaching - Anderson describes it as a measurable 'push harder and push longer' drill.

drills.name: Elevated knight-to-tripod shin-roll drill
drills.setup: Half-kneeling (elevated knight) position, then into a tripod.
steps: Start in an elevated half-kneeling lunge with hip extensors pre-activated.
Rock forward over the front foot (ankle rocker) as the shin rolls forward.
Move into the elevated tripod position slowly.
Then perform short wall drills / resisted marches emphasizing the same shin roll.
drills.dosage: 3 sets x 4-6 slow reps per side
drills.why: Slow, controlled practice of the shin roll and ankle rocker teaches the rotation-then-extension pattern before adding speed (from Alt's framework).

pro_tips.tip: Film acceleration at >=100 fps with the camera 6-10 m away to reduce perspective distortion, and compare key positions between legs to spot asymmetries.
Cue 'rock 'n' roll' (ankle rocker + shin roll) or 'kick your swing foot through your stance knee' to promote forward shin rotation.
Better accelerators orient their ground force more horizontally - technique of force application matters, not just strength.

skills.name: Maximal velocity mechanics
skills.recommended_camera: Side view, perpendicular, at 30-60 m mark, >=120 fps; panning or fixed camera ~10 m away.

checkpoints.description: Tall posture ('sprint tall'): hips high, trunk near vertical, head neutral.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: trunk within ~5-10 deg of vertical; hip height at mid-stance close to standing hip height

checkpoints.description: Step down from above: foot strikes the ground close to under the hips rather than reaching out in front.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: horizontal distance from touchdown ankle to hip vertical small (e.g., < ~30-40 cm at elite speeds); shin near vertical at touchdown

checkpoints.description: Short ground contact time and high step rate characterize maximal velocity; elite athletes balance step length and frequency differently.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: ground contact roughly 0.08-0.11 s at elite speeds (measure frames on/off); step frequency ~4.3-5.0 Hz in elite 100 m finalists

checkpoints.description: Front-side mechanics: the swing thigh comes through quickly and high in front while the back-side kick is limited.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: swing thigh approaches ~horizontal in front at toe-off of the opposite leg

checkpoints.description: Relaxed, linear arm action from the shoulder; hands don't cross the midline.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: wrists stay on their own side of the body midline in the front view

faults.name: Overstriding at top speed
faults.video_signs: Foot reaches out ahead of the body with a long, braking contact.
faults.why_it_matters: Anderson designed the wicket drill as a reaction to 'epidemic overstriding'.

faults.name: Sitting / low hips (back-side mechanics)
faults.video_signs: Hips sink, trunk leans forward or back, long backside recovery behind the body.
faults.why_it_matters: A collapsed posture lengthens ground contact and reduces force application.

faults.name: Tension and crossing arms
faults.video_signs: Shoulders shrugged, fists clenched, arms swinging across the body.
faults.correction_cue: 'Relax the face and shoulders; hands cheek to hip.'
faults.why_it_matters: Tension slows limb turnover; crossing arms creates rotation.

drills.name: V-Max wicket drill (Vince Anderson)
drills.setup: 6-inch mini-hurdles/slats placed with progressive spacing after a run-in (e.g., ~3'11" building to 5'5" wicket spacing for younger/developing athletes; ~4'4" to 5'10" for faster). Provide 2-3 lanes with different spacings.
steps: Accelerate through a 6-stride run-in into tall sprint posture BEFORE the wickets.
Run the wickets stepping down from above; don't look down - feel and listen.
Keep getting more; don't settle.
Run out past the last wicket to transfer the pattern.
drills.dosage: Start 2 x (12, 14, 16 strides), progress to 6 x 18 strides; 4-6 reps/session, 2-4 sessions/week; rest 2-3 min
drills.why: Spacing forces a set step length so athletes must step down under the body with good posture; Anderson cites 18 strides in ~3.65 s as excellent proficiency.

drills.name: Ins and Outs
drills.setup: Cone zones: ~25 m acceleration, then alternating 'in' (max) and 'out' (maintain) zones of 10-15 m (e.g., 70 m: 25 acc / 15 in / 15 out / 15 in).
steps: Accelerate aggressively.
'In' zones: maximal sprint.
'Out' zones: keep posture and rhythm/frequency, reduce only force into the ground ('freewheel' downhill).
Finish and coast.
drills.dosage: 2-3 x 70 m to start; 70-120 m, 2-6 reps; rest 5-10 min; introduce 6-7 weeks into training
drills.why: Alternating intensities while holding posture and frequency teaches relaxation at speed and posture retention.

pro_tips.tip: Elite 100 m finalists differ: in the London 2017 final Bolt averaged ~2.70 m steps at ~4.39 Hz while Coleman averaged ~2.33 m at ~4.95 Hz - there is no single ideal combination.
Maximal velocity is a major determinant of 100 m performance; it's trained with flying sprints (e.g., 20-40 m run-in, 10-30 m fly) and long recoveries.
